question:
A 24-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus is brought to the emergency department because of weakness, abdominal pain, nausea, and one episode of vomiting for 1 day. He has not taken his insulin for 3 days. His pulse is 125/min and respirations are 29/min. Examination shows dry mucous membranes. His breath has a fruity odor. Which of the following sets of laboratory values is most likely on evaluation of urine obtained before treatment?
 $$$ pH %%% HCO3- %%% NH4+ %%% K+ $$$?

paths: (Finding of blood glucose level)-PREDISPOSES->(Diabetes Mellitus, Insulin-Dependent)-INTERACTS_WITH->(Virus)-LOCATION_OF->(S100B)-PART_OF->(Adipose tissue)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Type 1 diabetes mellitus" -> "lack of insulin production" -> "increased blood glucose levels" -> "ketosis due to fat breakdown" -> "acidosis" -> "low pH in urine" -> "increased NH4+ in urine" -> "increased K+ in urine" -> "↓ ↓ ↑ ↑" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Insulin deficiency" -> "shift to anaerobic metabolism" -> "lactic acidosis" -> "low pH in urine" -> "increased NH4+ in urine" -> "increased K+ in urine" -> "↓ ↓ ↑ ↑" -> 90%
enhanced_information: In a 24-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus and insulin deficiency, the lack of insulin leads to increased blood glucose levels, ketosis, and subsequent acidosis. This results in low pH in urine, increased NH4+ in urine, and increased K+ in urine. Therefore, the most likely set of laboratory values on evaluation of urine obtained before treatment would be: ↓ ↓ ↑ ↑.
